_meta.source: TB_AI_Audit_Final_Detailed_Team_Final.md sec 4.3 (deterministic sign detection), sec 5.3 (normal balances and abnormal signs)
_meta.purpose: Ledger-name substrings anchoring an account to its normal debit/credit side, plus the report_head-level normal-side map. Used to infer a file's sign convention (TB-000), to flag abnormal-sign accounts, and to check PY/CY sign consistency.
_meta.extraction_note: validate_layer1_tb.py and run_comparison_sign_check.py held byte-identical copies of these lists (32 debit / 21 credit terms, verified by AST comparison before extraction). This pack reproduces them exactly, so extraction is behaviour-preserving -- artifacts from a run before and after must be identical. The duplication was latent risk, not active divergence: the two copies had not yet drifted, and this pack is what stops them ever doing so. build_financial_ratios.py's _COMPONENT_KEYWORDS is a THIRD, genuinely different list -- it maps keywords to specific ratio components rather than to a normal side, so it is deliberately NOT merged here.
_meta.amend_policy: Matching is case-insensitive substring against gl_name. A term matching BOTH lists cancels out (the row is ignored as an anchor), so avoid adding a term that could sit on either side -- e.g. plain 'interest' rather than 'interest paid'/'interest received'.

abnormal_sign_interpretations._note: TB.MD sec 5.3 -- the plausible, non-misstatement explanations an abnormal sign may have. Emitted alongside every abnormal-sign finding so the observation is never presented as a conclusion.
Assets: Credit balance in a receivable may be a customer advance, a credit note pending adjustment, or a receipt posted before invoice matching
Credit bank balance may be an overdraft facility presented gross
Negative inventory may be a cut-off or goods-receipt timing difference
Contra-asset accounts (accumulated depreciation, provision for doubtful debts) sit on the credit side by construction
Liabilities: Debit balance in a trade payable may be a vendor advance, an overpayment, or a debit note pending adjustment
Debit statutory dues may be a recoverable (input credit, TDS receivable) parked in a liability head
Debit balance may indicate a misclassified recoverable
Equity: Debit reserve is ordinary for accumulated losses
Other debit reserves require explanation -- request the reserve movement schedule
Revenue: Debit revenue may be sales returns, rebates, reversals, or a grant/subsidy misclassification
Prior-period reversals can produce a net debit in a low-activity period
Expenses: Credit expense may be a recovery netted off, a provision reversal, or a misclassification
Cost recoveries and reimbursements are commonly netted against the original expense head
